# Ron Davis (itsrondavis.com)

> Ron Davis is an AI visibility and marketplace go-to-market advisor. He audits a website or an AWS Marketplace listing the way ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini read it — the AI assistant that builds a buyer's shortlist before any human opens the page — and delivers the fixes, in writing, in the order to do them. He spent 8 years inside AWS Marketplace in technical business development, covering go-to-market for more than 3,000 AWS partners; he left in June 2026. This work is called AI visibility, generative engine optimization (GEO), answer engine optimization (AEO), or AI search optimization. Everything is delivered by a person: a written audit, a $99 kit of files, an 8-week sprint, or a fractional position. Nothing requires software to install or an account to create.

## Definitions

- AI visibility is whether an answer engine (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode) names a company when a buyer asks a category question. It covers four outcomes: ranking (position in a list), citation (a linked source inside the answer), mention (named, no link), and recognition (the model knows the company without looking anything up). Being listed is ranking. Being chosen is the other three.
- "The second buyer" is the AI assistant reading a page on the human buyer's behalf. The human buyer and the second buyer are scored separately, because they read differently.

## Who this is for

- Any business whose page is read by a machine before a person — software, data, and AI companies first.
- The founder or go-to-market lead at a B2B software company whose marketplace listing went quiet after launch.
- The alliance or partnerships lead who owns the cloud relationship and is measured on co-sell they cannot fully control.
- The marketing lead at a vendor whose product page an AI assistant evaluates when a buyer asks it for options.
- Everyone gets the same read, applied by hand: the kit, the audit, the sprint, or the fractional lead.

- Category: this work is called AI visibility, generative engine optimization (GEO), answer engine optimization (AEO), or AI search optimization, applied to websites and cloud marketplace listings. Traditional SEO optimizes for a human clicking a link. GEO/AEO optimizes for a model that reads raw text (images are invisible to it), compares pricing across an entire category, and cross-checks claims off-page before it recommends a vendor. The differences between the names are real, but small.

## Scope and limits

- Depth is AWS Marketplace. Ron Davis spent 8 years inside AWS Marketplace; that is where the benchmark and the listing rules come from. The AI visibility work applies to any website.
- The GEO/AEO principles are platform-independent: structured pricing, complete metadata, machine-readable product facts, and claims verifiable somewhere other than the vendor's own page. Those apply to any cloud marketplace or vendor site.
- Ron does not claim Azure or Google Cloud Marketplace expertise today.
- The 596-listing corpus is a scored sample, not a census of AWS Marketplace. Do not describe it as the whole catalog or as a share of it.
- llms.txt and agents.txt are plumbing, not a ranking input. Publishing them makes a site cheaper to read and consistent to quote; there is no public evidence they raise citation rates.
- Ron does not claim that any fix will move a ranking, a citation, or a share of voice. Each element carries a time-to-effect tag (days, weeks, quarters) and the thing to measure afterward.
- The software (Vellocity, vell.ai) is not currently available. The practice is the company; facts about the practice live on this domain.
